channel.title: Brazil Complexity — Research
channel.description: Independent research on the operational layer of Brazilian markets — for foreign investors, family offices, advisors, and operators evaluating a specific Brazilian decision.

item.title: Why Due Diligence Is Not Enough in Brazil
item.description: Standard due diligence confirms what is documented. In Brazil, the variables that determine whether a deal works are often not in the documents. The gap between formal DD and operational reality.

item.title: The Hidden Cost of Regulatory Geography in Brazil
item.description: In Brazil, the same activity is regulated differently depending on where it happens. Ignoring this regulatory geography is one of the most expensive mistakes foreign investors make.

item.title: When the Spreadsheet Is Right but the Decision Is Wrong
item.description: A financial model can be internally perfect and still point to the wrong decision — when it is built at the wrong resolution. The analytical error behind many failed Brazilian investments.

item.title: Can Foreign Investors Own Healthcare Real Estate in Brazil?
item.description: Yes — but the permission question is the easy one. What determines whether foreign-owned healthcare real estate in Brazil performs is the operational layer beneath the ownership.

item.title: Why a Good Investment Thesis Can Fail Locally in Brazil
item.description: The thesis is right. The sector is right. The numbers work. And the deal still fails — because the thesis lived at the country level and the deal executed somewhere the thesis never described.

item.title: The Difference Between Research and Ground Truth in Brazil
item.description: National data describes Brazil accurately and the deal poorly. The gap between research and ground truth is where foreign investment decisions go wrong — and where verification pays.

item.title: Why Brazil Is Not One Healthcare Market
item.description: Brazilian healthcare is not one market. It fragments by municipality, and the fragmentation determines returns. What foreign investors must read first.

item.title: Before You Choose a Municipality in Brazil
item.description: The municipality where your Brazilian deal executes is a primary investment decision. What foreign investors must verify before committing capital.

item.title: The Yield the Index Cannot See — Brazil Complexity
item.description: Brazilian rents rise while sale prices stay flat. FipeZAP measures the wrong variable — every position calibrated against it inherits the error.

item.title: Medical Office Buildings in Brazil: Why the U.S. Framework Does Not Translate
item.description: American investors evaluating Brazilian medical office buildings often apply U.S. benchmarks for cap rates, activation, and lease structure. None of them transfer cleanly.

item.title: Medical Office Buildings Brazil: Foreign Investor's MOB Guide
item.description: Why U.S. and European MOB frameworks fail in Brazil — cap rates, ANVISA regulatory risk, tenant mix, and activation cost rebuilt for the Brazilian market.

item.title: FipeZAP, IBRE, IGMI-C: Brazilian Real Estate Benchmarks
item.description: What FipeZAP, IBRE/FGV, and IGMI-C actually measure — and where Brazil's main real estate indices miss the yield foreign capital cares about.

item.title: FipeZAP and the Limits of Brazilian Real Estate Benchmarks
item.description: FipeZAP is Brazil's most widely cited real estate index. Here is what it measures, what it misses, and why foreign investors should use it carefully.

item.title: Brazilian Real Estate Beyond São Paulo: Foreign Investor Guide
item.description: Why durable yield in Brazil is increasingly found outside São Paulo and Rio — what foreign investors need to know about secondary cities and the South.

item.title: Brazil Tax Reform and the Foreign Investor: Why Structure Still Matters
item.description: Brazil's tax reform changes the regulatory landscape. It does not change the principle that structure is a primary investment decision — or that default has a cost.

item.title: Brazil Tax Reform 2026: Foreign Investor's Guide to IBS, CBS
item.description: Brazil's biggest tax reform in decades is live. What foreign investors need to know about IBS, CBS, IRPFM, ITCMD, and capital structure decisions.

item.title: Why Foreign Investors Fail in Brazil
item.description: Most foreign investment failures in Brazil are not failures of macro thesis. They are failures of operational analysis applied to a correct thesis.

item.title: Regulated Sectors Brazil: Legal Permission vs. Feasibility
item.description: In Brazil's regulated sectors, legal permission is not operational feasibility. The gap between the two is where most foreign investor failures occur.

item.title: Municipal Licensing Risk in Brazil
item.description: Brazil has 5,570 municipalities implementing federal rules differently. Municipal licensing is the most underestimated variable in foreign investment.

item.title: Local Partners in Brazil: The Hidden Market Entry Risk
item.description: Access and alignment differ. Most Brazil partnership failures were visible before capital was committed — if investors knew what to look for.

item.title: How to Scope a Brazil Complexity Brief
item.description: What a Brazil Complexity Brief covers, what it does not, and how to determine whether your situation warrants one. A guide to the most useful format of inquiry.

item.title: Healthcare Real Estate in Brazil: The Activation Layer
item.description: Why clinical real estate in Brazil is mispriced — and what activation, ANVISA compliance, and Vigilância Sanitária actually require from investors.

item.title: Complexity Arbitrage in Brazil: A Framework for Investors
item.description: How Brazil's jurisdictional fragmentation creates pricing inefficiencies — and why investors who engage the operational layer capture returns others miss.

item.title: Clinical Real Estate Brazil: Healthcare Property & Licensing
item.description: Why clinical real estate is persistently mispriced in Brazil — and what ANVISA RDC 50, Vigilância Sanitária, and municipal licensing actually determine.

item.title: Brazil Real Estate Investment: Why Benchmarks Miss True Yield
item.description: Why foreign investors in Brazilian real estate rarely see the yield they modeled — and what listing prices, FipeZAP, and cap rate comparables cannot tell you.

item.title: Brazil Real Estate Investment: Listing Prices vs. Actual Yield
item.description: FipeZAP describes what sellers ask, not what assets yield. Activation cost, licensing, and lease structure determine actual Brazilian real estate returns.

item.title: Brazil Market Entry: The Operational Layer Investors Miss
item.description: Why foreign investors who read Brazil correctly still fail — and what entry analysis actually requires. The operational layer public research cannot see.

item.title: Brazil Market Entry Is Not Market Research
item.description: Why foreign investors entering Brazil need more than market research — and what market entry analysis actually requires.

item.title: Brazil Beyond São Paulo and Rio: Why Execution Geography Matters
item.description: The Brazil most institutional research describes is the Brazil of São Paulo and Rio. The Brazil where durable yield opportunities exist is often somewhere else.

item.title: Why Brazil Disappoints the Passive Investor — Brazil Complexity
item.description: Brazilian equities rallied in 2025 yet passive capital captured little. The opportunity is in the operational layer that public benchmarks cannot measure.
